title: The meaning of the jama‘ah and praying in congregation
intro: The jama‘ah is the Muslim community – and the rows of Salah are the best picture of its strength.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: The believing men and women are allies of one another: they call to good and forbid evil, establish prayer, give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah will have mercy on them – Allah is Almighty, All-Wise. <small>(Qur’an, At-Tawbah 9:71)</small>

The jama‘ah is the Muslim community in which Muslims respect, love, help and advise one another. The word comes from an Arabic word meaning to gather and unite; from the same root comes the word jami‘ (masjid) – Allah’s house where Muslims gather to worship Him.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “Whoever wants the middle of Jannah, let him stay with the jama‘ah, for Shaytan is with the one who is alone, and further from two…” (Tirmidhi)

Showing the value of community, the Prophet (SAW), when he came to Madinah, built the Madinah community and its masjid. Its purpose was to grow love for Allah and His Messenger and brotherly love between the Muhajirun and the Ansar – the masjid was the place where they worked together and helped one another.

The jama‘ah and the masjid are very important in a Muslim’s life: places of peace and harmony, where good work and journeys begin, where problems a person can’t solve alone are solved, places of advice and brotherly love. Allah tells us: The believers are but brothers. (Qur’an, Al-Hujurat 49:10)

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) always prayed in jama‘ah and said: “Prayer in congregation is worth twenty-seven times more than prayer alone.” (Bukhari)

learn.text: The meaning of praying in jama‘ah

items: it teaches us that people are social beings, and our coming into the world, life and going to the akhirah are tied to a community
standing in rows shows the strength of the community and grows a feeling of unity
standing in a row reminds us that we are equal before Allah, whatever our colour, race or wealth
it teaches cleanliness, hygiene, punctuality and accuracy
praying together grows love, compassion and mercy among Muslims
the time before and after Salah is a chance to talk and help those with problems
the rows remind us of standing before Allah on the Day of Judgement
only a strong community that cares for each member and is united guarantees success for each of us

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Since Islam has existed, the jama‘ah has existed. Every link in the chain gives the jama‘ah strength. The rows are the best picture of the jama‘ah’s strength.

practice.title: What does praying in jama‘ah teach us?

options.why: The time before and after Salah is a chance to help and talk with others.

options: The Muslim community that loves and helps each other

questions.q: What did the Prophet (SAW) do first when he came to Madinah?
options: Built the community and its masjid

questions.q: How much more is prayer in congregation worth?
Where is the unity of the jama‘ah seen most clearly?
What does standing in rows remind us of?
options: Standing before Allah on the Day of Judgement

practice.title: Talk and tasks
prompts: 🕌 How many Muslims in your jama‘ah regularly pray the five prayers and come to the masjid?
🤝 Describe the relationships among Muslims in your jama‘ah. What would you change or improve?
📖 Talk with your muallim: “Hold firmly together to the rope of Allah and do not be divided.” (Qur’an, Ali ‘Imran 3:103)
